purpose: Compare three fixed aperture/deblending rules on the ten preregistered development singleton anchors while keeping all five validation anchors unmeasured and masked before source detection.

split.rule: Only development-anchor cutouts may be measured. Every known validation coordinate is masked before background estimation and source detection, including on mixed detector images.

measurement.background_model: Iteratively three-sigma-clipped affine plane using at least 100 finite, non-validation pixels.
measurement.psf_scale: Use the calibrated detector FWHM header, falling back only to the primary-header seeing divided by WCS pixel scale.
measurement.segmentation: PSF-smoothed positive-source islands split by watershed peaks; the fixed anchor coordinate is always the target marker and all other regions are contaminants.

variant_definitions.raw: Sum every finite background-subtracted aperture pixel without deblending.
variant_definitions.area_scaled: Mask non-target watershed pixels and scale the remaining sum by total-to-clean aperture area.
variant_definitions.rotate180: Replace each masked pixel with its unmasked point-reflection about the fixed target coordinate; area-scale only the still-unrecoverable pixels.

measurement.calibration: magnitude = primary-header MAGZERO - 2.5 log10(positive aperture flux)
measurement.retention: Process every one of the 670 development measurement memberships. A failed or non-positive measurement remains an explicit non-finite row and cannot remove its exposure or object.

development_ranking.rule: Lexicographically maximize the count of development objects with complete griz, maximize valid measurement fraction, minimize median repeated-exposure robust magnitude scatter, minimize leave-one-object-out Bessel-to-DECam color error, then minimize absolute difference from the existing four-arcsecond catalog aperture as a calibration diagnostic.

claim_boundary: V19AS is development-only measurement commissioning, not a validation result and not a baryonic mass, lensing, halo or gravity test.
The five validation anchors remain unmeasured. Their coordinates are used only to exclude their pixels before development background estimation and segmentation.
The 180-degree rule assumes local point symmetry and may be biased for intrinsically asymmetric galaxies; validation and injection tests are required before scientific use.
A winning development variant only recommends one exact rule for a separately frozen validation run. It does not authorize ambiguous-member association or a mass-current map.
